content: Open a new scene in Blender [k]Ctrl-N,G[/k]. [k]Delete[/k] the Camera and Light.

image.caption: Image 1 - Delete the default Camera and Light

content: Go to the Shading workspace and click the Cube. This will bring up the default material (Image 2). We want to use assign Imphenzia's palette for the default material (Image 3). This palette is 8x8 and takes up very little memory. With Blender and File Explorer open, drag the palette file into Shader Editor. Connect the palette's Image Texture Node's color output to the Principled BSDF's Base Color input (Image 4). It will be blurry on the cube, since it's been shrunk down to a small size; change the Image Texture Node's Interpolation to Closest (Image 5).

image.caption: Image 4 - Connecting the palette to the material shader
Image 5 - Changing the Image Texture Node's Interpolation to Closest

content: Open the Viewport Shading options and change the Color source to Texture (Image 6). Go down and enable Cavity. Set the Type to Both and bring up the Ridge and Valley values to maximum (Image 7).

image.caption: Image 6 - Change the Color source to Texture
Image 7 - Enable Cavity and modify the default setting

content: [k]Tab[/k] into Edit Mode and open the Tool Settings Options; enable Auto Merge (Image 8).
